newsitem.title: USA: Fed says banks ease terms on business loans.
newsitem.headline: Fed says banks ease terms on business loans.

text.p: Many banks are responding to stiff competition for commercial loans by easing lending terms, according to a survey of senior loan officers at large commercial banks issued Monday by the Federal Reserve.
But at the same time, they were tightening standards on credit-card loans and they observed that more consumers were substituting home-equity loans for other types of credit.

"Many of the respondents reported that they had eased terms on business loans over the past three months, citing pressure from other banks and nonbanks as the cause," the survey of 55 large banks found.

While banks were "competing aggressively" on loan terms, only a few said they relaxed their standards for applicants to qualify for credit. A small majority of survey respondents reported rising loan demand from large and medium-sized businesses, but several said small companies were more actively seeking loans.

The Fed surveys loan officers about every three months. The last similar survey, issued on Nov. 18, noted some pullback in consumer loan demand. The new survey similarly said there has been a recent slowdown in consumer loan growth but a marked pickup in home-equity loans.
The Fed said that bankers reported a recent rapid rise in demand for home equity loans, apparently in part because they were being substituted for unsecured forms of consumer credit.
"This shift reportedly has arisen from bank promotion of such substitution as well as from the initiative of borrowers attempting to consolidate their debt," the survey said.
The Fed noted that it was the fifth consecutive survey in which a significant percentage of banks had tightened standards on consumer loans.
"Nearly 40 percent of the banks, on net, said they had tightened standards ... for approving new credit card accounts, and 20 percent tightened standards on other consumer loans," the survey said.

Credit-card terms were toughened, with 25 percent of the survey respondents reporting that they had lowered credit limits, while 10 percent said they had increased the spread on these loans and on other consumer loans.
Banks said they had slightly tightened their standards for approving home mortgages since late last year and said mortgage loan demand had picked up moderately since then.
